newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX index jumps to new high, futures firm.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX index jumps to new high, futures firm.

text.p: The Hungarian share market followed its own way on Monday, moving into record territory as foreign investors, who were heavy sellers recently, entered the buying side of the market, traders said.

The BUX index closed at 5,572.80 points, up 103.97. The previous high of 5,499.74 points was reached on January 28. BUX futures closed higher for all maturities, with the March instrument outpacing others by jumping 135 points to 5,930.

"(On the spot market) investors seem to have pumped fresh money into the market," said Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securities. "Today, not only domestic investors but foreigners were also very active."
He said investors were apparently ready to pay any price for the papers.
"Orders to be met at market price dominated the market," Berecz said. "Sometimes I had the feeling that a 'buy-at-any-price' sentiment dominated."
Chemicals company TVK and oil company MOL were the most actively traded papers, while pharmaceuticals Richter came into focus with a huge deal for 100,000 shares at 11,000 forints per share.
TVK closed 2,590 forints, up 40, while MOL jumped to a new high of 3,500 forints before ending at 3,470, up 75.
Bullish sentiment pushed up a number of stocks, such as brewery Sopron and gas distributor Primagaz, both of which continued to benefit from corporate developments and plans, announced last week.
Both Sopron and Primagaz broke records already on Friday.

Sopron surged to a new record high of 5,000 forints, before easing to finish at 4,905 forints, up 505, on plans announced last week by its majority owner, Austria's Brau Union AG to merge Sopron with its other Hungarian unit Martfu.
Meanwhile Primagaz surged to a peak of 12,000 forints, before dropping to finish at 11,500, up 1,500.
However, there were also some stocks on the losing side.

Shares in liqueur maker Zwack plummeted more than 12 percent to close at 5,000 forints after trading in its shares was suspended just before the end of the session on Friday due to too fast an intraday rise.
